source: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/ — records read 14 Nov 2026; Kepler/Pioneer/Surveyor end-of-mission lines cross-checked on science.nasa.gov mission pages

items.name: Surveyor 3
items.story: A robot lander sent to prove a soft landing was possible. Two and a half years later Apollo 12 landed 180 m away; Conrad and Bean walked over and brought back about 10 kg of it, including the TV camera, now in the Smithsonian.

items.name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle (descent stage) + EASEP
items.ended: EASEP stopped accepting commands 27 Aug 1969; retroreflector still in use
items.story: The landing stage became the launch pad and stayed. The seismometer listened for moonquakes; the retroreflector still bounces lasers back to Earth.

items.name: Apollo 12 ALSEP
items.rest: Oceanus Procellarum, within ~180 m of Surveyor 3
items.ended: Shut down with all ALSEP stations, 30 Sep 1977
items.story: A nuclear-powered (SNAP-27 RTG) science station. Its seismometer recorded the first artificial moonquake when the ascent stage was crashed into the Moon.

items.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Module Falcon, LRV + ALSEP
items.ended: ALSEP shut down 30 Sep 1977; the rover is parked where it stopped
items.story: The first car on the Moon, used to explore within about 5 km of the lander. After the last EVA Scott dropped a hammer and a feather; they fell together.

items.name: Viking 1 Lander
items.story: The first U.S. lander to work on Mars, powered by two plutonium RTGs; it ran for more than six years.

items.name: Viking 2 Lander
items.ended: Turned off 11 Apr 1980 when its batteries failed
items.story: Viking 1's twin, landed on the opposite side of the planet.

items.name: Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner
items.rest: Ares Vallis, 19.33 N, 33.55 W (Sagan Memorial Station)
items.story: Bounced to a landing on airbags and released Sojourner, the first rover on Mars.

items.name: Spirit (MER-A)
items.story: Opportunity's twin. With one dead wheel it got stuck in soft soil and could not tilt its panels toward the Sun for winter.

items.name: Opportunity (MER-B)
items.story: Built for 90 sols, Opportunity worked for more than 5,000. Its final signal followed a planet-wide dust storm.

items.name: Phoenix Mars Lander
items.story: Dug into polar ground rich in water ice. As the Arctic summer ended it ran out of sunlight.

items.name: InSight
items.ended: Last transmission 15 Dec 2022; declared over 21 Dec 2022
items.story: A seismometer on Mars: it listened for marsquakes to map the planet's interior, until dust starved its solar panels.

items.name: Ingenuity helicopter (Mars 2020)
items.ended: Rotors damaged on its flight of 18 Jan 2024; no longer able to fly
items.story: The first powered, controlled flight on another planet (19 Apr 2021, 39.1 s). Now a stationary monument.

items.name: NEAR Shoemaker
items.ended: Final contact 28 Feb 2001; still lying on Eros
items.story: The first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid, and then the first to land on one. It was never designed to land at all: after a year circling Eros the team brought it down anyway on 12 Feb 2001, and it survived the touchdown and kept transmitting from the surface for over two weeks.

items.name: Dawn
items.rest: Unpowered orbit around Ceres; expected to stay up about 50 years
items.ended: Out of hydrazine; last contact 31 Oct 2018
items.story: The first spacecraft to orbit two worlds beyond Earth: the giant asteroid Vesta for 14 months from 2011, then the dwarf planet Ceres from 2015. When its hydrazine ran out it was deliberately left in a high, stable orbit rather than allowed to fall — NASA will not risk contaminating Ceres with anything from Earth. The team put it better than 99% certain it will still be circling in about fifty years.

items.name: Kepler Space Telescope
items.ended: Retired after running out of fuel (2018), left in its safe orbit away from Earth
items.story: Stared at one patch of sky to catch planets crossing their stars.

items.name: Pioneer 10
items.story: First to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter. Heading the opposite way to the Voyagers.

items.name: Pioneer 11
items.ended: Science operations and daily telemetry ceased 30 Sep 1995
items.story: Flew past Jupiter and became the first spacecraft to visit Saturn.

items.name: Voyager 1
items.story: A deep-space counterpoint: Voyager 1 was never abandoned and is still answering from interstellar space.
